sheet-2.description: Downtown Somerville around the courthouse district, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 70 degrees, so that north lies toward the right of the page and West Main Street runs down the middle. West Main Street is lined with the principal commercial blocks: the Somerville Trust Co. bank and the Public Library with its fire department quarters on the east side of the street, and on the west side a continuous row of brick stores, a furniture store, drug stores, a hardware store, printing shops, the Post Office with a Dime Bank, and the Teneyck Hotel at the Division Street corner. The Waldorf Hotel with a bowling alley and the Somerville Publishing Co. stand at the top left. At the top the Buick garage, the 2nd Reformed Church and the large Sargent Bros., Inc. lumber yard and planing mill with its sheds occupy the block between Davenport Street and West Main Street, with the Church of the Immaculate Conception and its rectory beside West High Street at the upper right. Most of the right-hand side, between Maple Street and North Bridge Street, is frame dwellings with a few brick houses. The lower left holds the Second National Bank, the Hotel Crowley, a bottling works and wagon sheds. Water pipes of 6 to 10 inches run along the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at the corners. A compass rose with a north arrow is printed at the right, and a scale bar at the bottom. Adjoining sheets are numbered at the margins (3, 4, 5, 6, 9).
notes: Division does not meet West Main Street in today's street network, so no junction was available at its west end.
Union Street and Division Street are partly rebuilt today around the post office and the station area.
Control points at the sheet edge (West High, Davenport, North Bridge, South) were hand-picked at the crossing of the printed water pipes, which run along the street centres.

50 ft, turned (north to the right, rotation 70): downtown W Main, Union, Davenport, Maple, W High, N Bridge, South, Division. Detector locked on lot lines; placed mostly on hand-picked water-pipe crossings (7 of 8 points).

sheet-3-1.description: The western end of downtown Somerville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. West Main Street runs up the middle of the sheet from Davenport Street at the bottom to its five-way junction with North and South Doughty Avenues, West End Avenue and Somerset Street. Hunterdon Street and West High Street run parallel at the right, and South Street and Elm Street lie at the left. The large works of the Cott A. Lapp Company, burlap wall fabric makers, fill the block between New Street, Somerset Street and South Doughty Avenue, with its main mill, boiler house, inclined trestle and a siding from the Central Railroad of New Jersey, whose line curves along the left edge; beside it stand the A. Hollander and Son fur dressing works and, at the left, the Redfern Lace Company buildings. West Main Street is commercial: the Culm Rock Spring Water Company, auto sales rooms, the Henry A. Dix and Sons uniform factory, the Regent Theatre motion picture house, the Somerville Garage, the Somerville Steam Laundry, a bakery, drug store, plumber and a large garage near Davenport Street. The Elks Lodge and Club, the Eagles Lodge rooms and the New Jersey State Police headquarters (Troop B) are on the blocks west of West Main Street. The rest of the sheet, along North Doughty Avenue, Hunterdon Street and West High Street, is frame dwellings. A scale of feet is drawn at the bottom. The upper left corner holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: The south-west of the sheet (South and Elm Streets, the Lapp works) was rebuilt around Veterans Memorial Drive and the station; no junction there survives.
North Doughty Avenue / West High Street lies just off the right edge; not used.
Cott A. Lapp Co., manufacturers of burlap wall fabrics, with a siding from the Central Railroad of New Jersey.

50 ft. Part 1: W Main / Doughty / West End / Somerset to Davenport, Hunterdon, W High; south-west corner (South, Elm) rebuilt around Veterans Memorial Drive. Part 2: inset top left, block 7 on Mountain Av between West End Av and W High (placed on two parcel block corners).

sheet-3-2.description: A small inset in the upper left corner of sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and set off from the main map by a heavy line, with its own north arrow. It shows block 7, bounded by West End Avenue at the left, Mountain Avenue running diagonally across the top and West High Street at the right, the corner of block 8 beyond Mountain Avenue, and the edge of block 3 below. The block holds a few frame dwellings, one of brick, with their stables and auto houses, on large lots facing Mountain Avenue and West High Street; most of the block is open ground. Street widths of 66 feet for West End Avenue and 80 feet for Mountain Avenue and West High Street are lettered, and 6, 8 and 12 inch water pipes are drawn in the streets with a fire hydrant at West End Avenue.
notes: Placed on two parcel block corners of the block (at West End Avenue and at West High Street, both on Mountain Avenue), as a two-point helmert; low confidence.

50 ft. Part 1: W Main / Doughty / West End / Somerset to Davenport, Hunterdon, W High; south-west corner (South, Elm) rebuilt around Veterans Memorial Drive. Part 2: inset top left, block 7 on Mountain Av between West End Av and W High (placed on two parcel block corners).

sheet-4.description: The southern edge of downtown Somerville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 78 degrees, so that north lies toward the right and East Main Street runs down the right side of the page. S. Bridge Street crosses the top, with Warren Street, Franklin Street and Centre Street running across the sheet and Hamilton Street closing it at the bottom. A multiple-track railroad, the Central Railroad of New Jersey, crosses the left side on a diagonal, with a signal station and a wooden bridge where Centre Street meets 1st St. East of the tracks the sheet is a mixed district of industry and trade. The Consumers Supply Co. and Chas. J. Smith and Co. coal yards with their sheds and trestles, a hay house, grain house, cement warehouse, lumber yards with a planing mill, junk yards, a wagon repository, and a printing office stand between the railroad and Franklin Street. The Cort Theatre, an armory-sized garage and auto sales and service buildings, a fire department house and the Somerville Athletic Ass'n club house with a bowling alley face Warren Street and East Main Street. Dwellings are mostly frame, with a few brick houses along Franklin Street and S. Bridge Street, and there is a bottling house and a colored mission hall near Hamilton Street. Water pipes of 3 to 10 inches run in the streets. A compass rose is printed at the lower right and the scale bar at the bottom. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 2, 5, 6, 12 and 13 at the margins.
notes: Franklin Street south of Warren Street is Veterans Memorial Drive East today; Franklin Street north of Warren Street keeps the name.
Centre Street is now Center Street.
Control rests on five detected junctions; the east side of East Main Street has none, because hand-picked points on the water pipes of East Main Street disagreed with the fit by 5 to 9 m.
The railroad on the left was left out of the control (use_railroads false): the drawn tracks lay 21 m from the modern line.

50 ft, turned (rotation 78): S Bridge, Franklin (now Veterans Memorial Drive East south of Warren), Warren, E Main, Grove, Mechanic, Hamilton, Centre. Railroad drawn 21 m off its modern line (rail control off); top right uncontrolled.

sheet-5.description: The courthouse district of Somerville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 19 degrees counter-clockwise, so that north lies toward the upper right. East High Street crosses the middle of the sheet, with N. Bridge Street down the left edge, Grove Street running up and down through the centre and right, E. Cliff Street along the top and E. Main Street along the bottom. The block between East High Street and East Main Street, numbered 24, is the Somerset County Court House grounds: the court house of 1907, built of fireproof construction, with the County Jail and Women's Department to its north, the 1st Reformed Church with its Sunday school across the grounds, and the Sheriff's house. East of Grove Street are the Co. M. Armory of the 2nd Reg. N.G.N.J., a garage for 30 cars, an auto show room, private garages and an auto repair shop, and the Somerset Hotel at East Main Street. The blocks north of East High Street, numbered 21 and 22, are made up of frame dwellings on long lots with a few outbuildings, set among large open back yards. Water pipes of 6 to 10 inches are shown in the streets and hydrants and fire alarm boxes stand at the corners. A compass rose with a north arrow is printed at the upper right. The adjoining sheets are numbered 2, 4, 9, 11 and 12 at the margins.
notes: Control rests on five detected junctions; fitted scale is 7.37 px/ft against about 7.6 on the other 50 ft sheets, about 3 percent small.
Grove Street bends near East Main Street in the modern data; the junction there was not detected.
50 ft (no printed scale; the fit confirms it, 3 to 5 percent small): N Bridge, E/W High, E Cliff, Grove, E Main, Warren, court house block.

sheet-6-1.description: The railroad district on the south side of downtown Somerville, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. South Street runs across the top of the sheet from Union Street past Division Street, which runs down to the tracks, and South Bridge Street runs down the right edge, with Franklin Street, 1st Street and 2nd Street meeting it from the east. Between South Street and the railroad lie small blocks along Wausau Place and a private way: dwellings and stores, the New Jersey Tobacco Company shipping building, a bottling house, an express office and, east of Division Street, the Commercial Hotel and a large garage for 40 cars. The middle of the sheet is the yard of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, with the passenger station on its north side, a freight house, tool houses and an elevated water tank. South of the tracks are coal and lumber dealers served by sidings: the W. S. Vroom Bridge Street Mill (flour, feed and coal), Sargeant Brothers coal shed, the Somerset Supply Company and Richards and Gaston Inc. with lumber sheds, a woodworking and machine shop, wagon sheds and an auto storage building beside South Bridge Street. Water pipes of 6 to 10 inches are shown in the streets. The lower left of the sheet holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: Union Street and Wausau Place south of Main Street no longer exist; the area is the station and Veterans Memorial Drive.
2nd Street is Second Street today.

Franklin Street / South Bridge Street and Second Street / South Bridge Street were hand-picked, and the old Union / South corner was carried from sheet 2; the fitted scale (about 7.35 px per ft) is about 4 percent below the other 50 ft sheets, so South Bridge Street may be drawn short or changed near the railroad.

50 ft. Part 1: South St, Division St, S Bridge St, Franklin St, 2nd St and the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard. Part 2: inset lower left, South St west of Union St along the railroad (area rebuilt; placed from the Union / South corner carried from part 1, which carries it from sheet 2; part 1 is held at its first-pass placement (second_pass keep)).

sheet-6-2.description: A small inset in the lower left corner of sheet 6, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and set off by a heavy line. It continues South Street westward from Union Street, beyond the left edge of the main map, and shows the strip between South Street and the main line of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which runs diagonally across the lower part of the inset. Block 12 holds a row of frame dwellings on South Street with stables behind, and at its western end the Swift and Company meat warehouse with cold storage rooms, an office, a shed and a coal house. Union Street, 40 feet wide, runs down the right edge of the inset. An 8 inch water pipe is drawn in South Street and a 6 inch pipe in Union Street.
notes: Swift and Co. meat warehouse with cold storage.
No street of the inset survives; placed from the South / Union corner carried from part 1, with the scale and rotation of part 1. Low confidence.

50 ft. Part 1: South St, Division St, S Bridge St, Franklin St, 2nd St and the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard. Part 2: inset lower left, South St west of Union St along the railroad (area rebuilt; placed from the Union / South corner carried from part 1, which carries it from sheet 2; part 1 is held at its first-pass placement (second_pass keep)).

sheet-7.description: The north-western edge of Somerville along West End Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north roughly up the page. West End Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the right edge, with Hillcrest Avenue, the borough line, running down the left edge and Bell Street branching from it. North Middagh Street and South Middagh Street run down the middle of the sheet to Somerset Street, which crosses the lower half from left to right, with Cammann Pl., Washington and New Streets and Mountain Av. as the other cross streets. The blocks numbered 101, 102 and 151 to 156 are largely frame dwellings on deep lots, with a few brick houses. The Redfern Lace Wks., a large brick mill with its own boilers, stands at the left; the 4th Reformed Church, a grain warehouse and a coal shed are along North Middagh Street, and Rite Made Shirt Wks. and The Cott-a-Lapp Co. are near New Street at the right. A. V. Norton Green Houses, with several glass houses, fill a block on Somerset Street, and Washington's Headquarters is shown in block 153. A railroad crosses the sheet on a diagonal from the left edge to the lower right, with a coal shed beside it. The upper right holds a club house in open ground, a compass rose and the printed scale note. Water pipes of 6 to 36 inches are marked, the 36 inch main running in Hillcrest Avenue. Much of the right and lower parts of the sheet is blank, being outside the built-up area.
notes: North Middagh is North Middaugh Street today; Hillcrest Avenue, along the borough line, is Cornell Boulevard.
The fitted scale is 4.07 px/ft, about 4 percent above the 3.9 of the other 100 ft sheets; spacing along Middaugh and Somerset Streets agrees with it.
Detected junctions on this sheet sat 40 to 55 ft off the street centres, so the control points are hand-picked at the crossings of the printed water pipes.
West End Avenue is drawn about 7 m from its modern line near Mountain Avenue; the junction there was left out.
Bell Street and North Middaugh Street do not meet in the modern data as drawn, so Bell was not used.

100 ft: west end, West End Av, Hillcrest Av, Bell, N/S Middagh, Cammann Pl, Somerset, New, Washington, railroad. Placed on 4 hand-picked pipe crossings and 1 detected point; fits 5 percent large (4.07 px/ft); weak, shares no junction with another sheet.

sheet-8-1.description: The north-western residential district of Somerville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. West End Avenue runs down the left edge and Hillcrest Avenue, along the borough line, crosses the upper left corner. North Middagh Street, Mountain Avenue, North Doughty Avenue and Mercer Street run diagonally up to the right, crossed by Altmont Place, West Cliff Street, West Summit Street, Prospect Street and West High Street. The blocks numbered 1, 2, 3, 50 to 52, 103 to 106 and 155 to 158 are almost entirely frame dwellings with private stables and auto houses on deep lots; a few houses are of brick. St. John's Protestant Episcopal Church, of stone, with its Sunday school and rectory, stands at West High Street in block 3, and a second Sunday school room is nearby. A brook crosses the open land of block 158 at the lower right under a small bridge. Water pipes of 4 to 36 inches are shown in the streets, including a 36 inch main in Hillcrest Avenue, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at the junctions. The scale is printed at the top right and a scale bar at the bottom. The lower left corner holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: North Middagh is North Middaugh Street today; Altmont Place is Altamont Place.
Hillcrest Avenue, along the borough line, is Cornell Boulevard today.
North Middaugh / West End and North Middaugh / Altamont were left out: hand-picked points there disagreed with the fit by 7 to 10 m (jogged junctions).
St. John's Protestant Episcopal Church with Sunday school and rectory.

100 ft. Part 1: N Middagh, Altmont Pl, W Summit, Prospect, Mountain Av, W Cliff, N Doughty, Mercer, West End Av. Part 2: inset lower left, Hillcrest Av (now Cornell Boulevard, borough line) at Prospect and W Summit.

sheet-8-2.description: A small inset in the lower left corner of sheet 8, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and set off by a heavy line, with its own north arrow. It shows Hillcrest Avenue, 100 feet wide and drawn along the borough line, crossing Prospect Street and West Summit Street at the north-western edge of Somerville. Block 154 above Hillcrest Avenue holds a single large frame dwelling, and block 155 below it a dwelling with a brick or stone wing and an auto house; the rest is open ground. Water pipes of 6 inches are drawn in Hillcrest Avenue, Prospect Street and West Summit Street, with a fire hydrant at West Summit Street. A dash-dot match line lettered A and B runs along the bottom of the inset.
notes: Hillcrest Avenue is Cornell Boulevard today.
Placed on two hand-picked junctions (Cornell Boulevard with West Summit and with Prospect Street), helmert; low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1: N Middagh, Altmont Pl, W Summit, Prospect, Mountain Av, W Cliff, N Doughty, Mercer, West End Av. Part 2: inset lower left, Hillcrest Av (now Cornell Boulevard, borough line) at Prospect and W Summit.

sheet-9.description: The residential and school district of north-west Somerville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 71 degrees, so that north lies toward the right of the page. Mercer Street crosses the top and Grove Street the bottom; W. High, W. Cliff and E. Cliff Streets run down the left and middle, with Davenport, Ross and N. Bridge Streets crossing them. Peters Creek winds from the upper right to the lower right with W. Summit and E. Summit Streets following its banks, and bridges carry Davenport, N. Bridge and Grove Streets across it; a concrete bridge is shown at the top. The centre-left holds the public institutions of the town: Public School No. 2, Public School No. 1 and the Central High School with its auditorium, all of brick and fireproof construction, with the Colored School nearby, the 1st M. E. Church, the 1st Baptist Church of Somerville and a church of St. Thomas. Elsewhere the blocks, numbered 4, 18, 19, 53, 54, 56, 57 and 159, are frame dwellings with stables and auto houses on narrow lots, with large tracts of open ground on the east side of the creek where W. Summit Street is marked not opened. Water pipes of 3 to 12 inches run in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at the corners. A compass rose with a north arrow is printed at the upper right, with the scale note, and a scale bar at the bottom. The adjoining sheets are numbered 2, 3, 5, 8, 10 and 11 at the margins.
notes: Control rests on 14 detected junctions with a fit of 3.9 m, larger than usual; residuals along Davenport Street grow toward the east, up to about 7 m, and the same street is drawn about 20 m off its modern line farther north on sheet 10.
The Davenport Street junctions with West Summit Street and Green Street were kept in the fit; leaving them out moved the other junctions by as much.
Green Street is drawn as West Green and East Green on either side of Peters Creek.
100 ft, turned (rotation 72): W Summit, W/E Cliff, Davenport, Mercer, Ross, N Bridge, Grove, Peters Creek.

sheet-10.description: A residential sheet north of downtown Somerville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. North Bridge Street runs across the middle of the sheet, with Davenport Avenue parallel to it along the top and Grove Street along the bottom. West Green, West Spring, Brown and Richard Streets cross between Davenport Avenue and North Bridge Street, with a further unnamed street beyond them, and East Green and East Spring Streets continue the grid between North Bridge and Grove Streets. The blocks numbered 160 to 165 and 198 to 202 are only partly built up: frame dwellings with small stables and auto houses stand mostly along North Bridge Street, the lower end of Davenport Avenue and the Spring Streets, while the upper blocks toward the borough line are largely empty lots. At the right, beyond North Bridge Street, lies the Ross Farm, drawn with a farmhouse, a barn, corn cribs, coops and several poultry houses; the borough line runs down the sheet at the right. A creek (Peters Brook) crosses the bottom of the sheet below Grove Street, where a few dwellings back onto it in block 202. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are shown in North Bridge, Grove and Davenport. Fire hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked along the main streets. The scale bar and a north arrow are drawn on the sheet.
notes: Richard Street on the sheet is West Orchard Street today, by its position on North Bridge Street.
The unnamed street beyond Richard is in the position of West Young Street.
Davenport Avenue north of Brown Street is drawn about 20 m off the line of modern Davenport Street; junctions there were not used.
Davenport / West Spring was hand-picked; the detector paired a lot line there.
100 ft: N Bridge, Davenport Av, W Green, W/E Spring, Brown, Richard (now Orchard), Grove. Davenport north of Brown is drawn off its modern line (hand-pick there disagreed by 20 m; left out).

sheet-11.description: A residential and open-land district on the north side of Somerville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, so that streets running north-south on the ground run across the page. Grove Street crosses the top of the sheet and the brook runs beneath it by a concrete bridge. Peters Brook enters at the left, joins a second branch and crosses the sheet from lower left to right, passing under William Street by a small bridge. Culver Street crosses the middle of the sheet and North Gaston Avenue lies below it; Bartine, William and Catherine Streets run between them, and East Cliff Street runs down the left edge to Eastern Avenue at the foot. East Spring Street and Brown Street are drawn at the top right. Frame dwellings with a few stables and auto houses stand along Grove Street, East Cliff Street, North Gaston Avenue and Eastern Avenue; blocks 177, 180 to 183, 185, 187 and 202 are otherwise largely vacant, with deep lots laid out and two streets marked as proposed at the right. The only works shown is the former Somerville Brick Works in block 202, whose buildings are marked old and not in operation. A garage with a concrete floor and steam heat stands in block 181 beside North Gaston Avenue. Water pipes of 6 inches run in the streets, with hydrants, a fire alarm box at Culver Street and a fire alarm box on Grove Street. The title cartouche, a north arrow and the scale bar are printed on the sheet, and the adjoining sheets 5, 9, 10, 12 and 14 are numbered at the edges.
notes: Catharine is Catherine Street today; the two streets marked Proposed St. at the right (blocks 183 and 185) are not built as drawn.
The street running down the page from William at North Gaston Avenue to Eastern Avenue is Union Avenue in OpenStreetMap; no name was read for it on the sheet.

North Gaston / William and Culver / East Cliff were left out of the fit: the modern junction nodes sit 9 to 10 m from where the drawn streets meet. Catherine / North Gaston and Grove / William, hand-picked, each disagreed with the fit by more than 10 m and were not used.
The fit has few points and its scale is about 2 percent under the 3.9 px/ft of the other sheets; the Grove Street end rests on extrapolation.

100 ft, turned (rotation 76): Grove, Culver, William, Bartine, Catharine, N Gaston Av, E Cliff, Eastern Av, Peters Brook, former Somerville Brick Works. William continues south of N Gaston as today's Union Avenue (unlettered).

sheet-12.description: The central and north-eastern part of Somerville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top and slightly to the left. East Main Street crosses the sheet from left to right at its middle, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey runs along the foot. Peters Creek winds down the sheet from the top, passing under concrete bridges at East High Street and East Main Street. East High Street and East Cliff Street cross the upper half, with Culver Street joining them, and North Gaston Avenue and Eastern Avenue run across the page. South of East Main Street, South Gaston Avenue runs down to Central Avenue past Fairview Avenue, with Loser Avenue at the right. Coddington Place lies between East High and East Main Streets, and Park Avenue runs diagonally to East Main Street at the lower left, beside Mechanic and Hamilton Streets. Most of the sheet is frame dwellings on narrow deep lots. The Lafayette Public School stands in block 108 at North Gaston Avenue. Sisser Bros. Inc., express and furniture warehouse, occupies a large brick building on East Main Street, with a synagogue and a row of tile-walled dwellings on Park Avenue. A Public Service Corporation electric sub-station and storage stand at the foot of Hamilton Street, and an auto painting shop is on South Gaston Avenue. A casino building is drawn at the right edge. Large blocks 174, 27 and 23 1/2 along the creek are mostly open. The compass rose and north arrow are at the upper left, the scale bar at the bottom, and the neighbouring sheets 4, 5, 11, 13 and 14 are numbered at the edges.
notes: Peter's Creek is Peters Brook today; Coddington Place is Codington Place; Loser Avenue is Loeser Avenue.
Franklin appears lettered both as FRANKLIN and as FRANKLIN ST. where it meets Hamilton.
East Main Street meets North Gaston Avenue and South Gaston Avenue at two nodes about 20 m apart, as drawn.
100 ft: E Cliff, E High, E Main, Culver, Park Av, Mechanic, Hamilton, Franklin, N/S Gaston Av, Coddington Pl, Fairview, Central, Eastern, Loser Av, Peter's Creek.

sheet-13.description: The south-eastern residential district of Somerville, below the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right, so that streets running north-south on the ground cross the page. South Bridge Street runs along the top, rising slightly to the right, with Centre Street and Hamilton Street below it, all crossed by 3rd Street, 2nd Street and 1st Street, and by South Side Avenue at the left. Blocks 58 to 62 and 172 are the built-up area, almost entirely frame dwellings on narrow deep lots facing 3rd and 2nd Streets, with a fire alarm box at Centre Street. At the lower right a block between 2nd Street and 1st Street holds the Standard Oil Company oil station with tanks and a wagon shed and the Public Service Corporation gas station with its gasometer, store house and a fire-proof building. A strip of unbuilt ground marked Rika, with the note arbitrary, runs down the left side. The left third of the sheet is open land, with a cemetery lettered at the left edge, and blocks 66, 16, 172 and 173 carry only a few scattered buildings. The right edge shows the Central Railroad of New Jersey on a multi-track line crossing 1st Street on a bridge. A compass rose with the north arrow is at the upper left, the scale bar is at the lower left and the adjoining sheets 4, 6 and 12 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Centre Street is Center Street today; South Side Avenue is Southside Avenue.
The strip lettered Rika and ARBITRARY at the left is drawn as a strip with the note arbitrary; no modern street was matched to it.
The drawn 2nd Street, 3rd Street and Centre Street are matched to OpenStreetMap Second Street, 3rd Street and Center Street.
Hamilton / South Side Avenue rests on a single measured edge arm and has a residual of about 4 m.
100 ft, turned (rotation 70): south of the railroad, S Bridge, Centre, Hamilton, 1st to 3rd St, South Side Av, Rika (arbitrary), cemetery; left third uncontrolled.

sheet-14.description: The north-eastern part of Somerville between East Main Street and the Central Railroad of New Jersey, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top and slightly to the left. East Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet and Fairview Avenue and Central Avenue lie below it, with the railroad running along the foot. Eastern Avenue, Vanderveer Avenue, Renell Avenue, James Street and Haynes Street run down the page, with Loser Avenue at the lower left, and East High Street and Grant Avenue cross the upper half. Dwellings line Eastern Avenue and East High Street, and the large blocks 188 to 190, 192, 194, 213 and 214 above East Main Street are mostly open land with a few houses and barns. Below East Main Street are rows of frame dwellings on blocks 115 and 116, the Somerset Hospital with a nurses' home in block 116, and the Somerville Iron Works, manufacturers of pipes and castings, with its foundry, machine shop and pattern storage on Fairview Avenue and James Street. The Somerville Stove Works stands beside it at the right and Gunzelmaw and Cramer's lumber and mill work, with a lumber storage building and cement sheds, is at the lower left on Central Avenue. The compass rose and north arrow are at the upper right, the title cartouche and scale note are at the top right and the scale bar is at the foot. The neighbouring sheets 11, 12 and 15 are numbered at the margins, and a dashed East Cliff Street is lettered at the upper left.
notes: Renell Avenue is Rehill Avenue today; Loser is Loeser Avenue.
East Cliff Street is lettered E. CLIFF ST. at the upper left, beside Eastern Avenue, as a dashed street.
Somerville Iron Works, with its foundry and machine shop, and the Somerville Stove Works; the lumber firm is lettered Gunzelmaw and Cramer.
The first-order fit rests on junctions east of Eastern Avenue only; the Central Avenue and railroad edge was not used as control.
100 ft: Eastern Av, Vanderveer Av, Renell Av (now Rehill Avenue), E High, Grant Av, E Main, Fairview, James, Haynes, Loser Av, Central Av; Somerville Iron Works, Stove Works, Somerset Hospital.

sheet-15-1.description: The eastern edge of Somerville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top. East Main Street runs across the lower part of the sheet; north of it Eastern States Boulevard (Eastern Parkway) runs diagonally up the left side and Clark Avenue, Richards Avenue, Auten Avenue and Adamsville Avenue run north to East High Street, East Cliff Street and East Putnam Street. Grant Avenue meets Eastern States Boulevard from the west, and Haynes and Van Doren Avenue run south from East Main Street at the lower left. Only the blocks along East Main Street and those at Haynes and Van Doren Avenue are built up, with frame dwellings, stables and a few small stores; the blocks numbered 207 to 209, 223 to 225 and 235 are open land, and East Cliff and East Putnam Streets and the upper parts of the avenues are drawn with dashed lines as streets laid out but not opened. The borough line runs down the right edge along Adamsville Avenue. The upper left corner holds two small separate insets, not part of this map.
notes: East High Street on the sheet is Adams Street today.
East Cliff and East Putnam are dashed paper streets drawn 25 to 50 m from the modern Madison and Putnam Streets; not used.
Adamsville Avenue is North Adamsville Road; Eastern States Boulevard is Eastern States Parkway.

100 ft. Part 1: E Main with Haynes, Van Doren, Eastern States Blvd, Clark, Richards, Auten, Adamsville; E High is Adams Street today; E Cliff and E Putnam are dashed paper streets drawn 25 to 50 m off the modern Madison and Putnam Streets (left out). Parts 2 and 3: two small insets top left (block 205, former Pest House on Davenport; block 206, former Orphans Home on Lenox Av), not placed.
